To me, Kingdom Come: Deliverance II is a stronger game than even Baldur’s Gate 3. Warhorse’s vision of Bohemia carries an almost unprecedented sense of being lived-in—a world that keeps turning slowly, quietly, in conversations one’ll never hear, in bricks and timber steeped in the flow of history. One can feel that history stretching across towns and villages, in the lives of ordinary people struggling to survive amidst wars they have no power to stop.

Mark von Aulitz asks: [spoiler]‘How are you any different from Sigismund’s army?’ — ‘I was just doing what I had to do.’[/spoiler] But is that really true? Invaders pillage and burn in the name of some idealised homeland, whispering to themselves at night that ‘it’s for the good of the country’, and somehow find it in themselves to be cruel to lives they’ve never known. That's why Henry replies: [spoiler]‘We are not the same.’[/spoiler]

And me—I watched the unbroken spirits of Suchdol’s people, their resilience and courage in the face of despair, and found myself in tears amidst their cries.

This game starts you off with rags on your back, no food, no bed, no horse, you stink, thrown in the stocks, no weapon, and you have 5 groschen to your name. And I love it. 

From the simplicity of Troskowitz, and the greater Trosky region, to the cinematic scenes in Kuttenberg, this game delivers on all fronts. 

Personally, after two playthroughs, I prefer the Trosky region. It feels more immersive than Kuttenburg where the stakes get greater. I enjoyed sticking my nose in everyone's business from Tachov, Zhelleov, Semine, Troskowitz, and everywhere in between. 

The Wedding was awesome. Cool to see that your interactions amongst the villages mentioned above actually matter when you get to the wedding. It didn't disappoint. 

The Kuttenburg map does feel a little too big but I'm not losing sleep over it. It just doesn't have the same small personality that Trosky does with the bickering and feuding villages. 

The main story was great. I missed out on KCD1 so some moments didn't pack as big a punch as they could have, but that's my fault and not the game. Good job getting the player up to date with passing comments regarding KCD1. 

Side quests are up there with The Witcher 3 in terms of quality and substance. No dumb Bethesda fetch quests for the most part. Bad Blood right off the rip gives you a good taste for what they can achieve. 

The characters are super memorable. From Henry and Capon to Dry Devil and Adder. Great job with a large ensemble. 

Gameplay is very fun. I've never had more fun with alchemy in a game. Highly recommend getting the Henry quality potions early on so you can craft Henry's Fox and reap the rewards. The game is so immersive that it really does encourage you to be self sufficient whether that means hunting for food and levelling your survivor skill, or crafting a number of potions, crafting your own weapons, etc. Typically that doesn't do much for me in games but this one had me by the pizzle and I took every chance to level my Henry up as much as I could and it rarely felt a burden. 

You do eventually get OP in many facets of the game and these small moments where you level up are not as meaningful as they are in the first 20 hours but what're you donna do. 

Nitpicks: 
-Need to add more voice actors. There's a lot of minor NPCs that have the same voice actor as a substantial NPC and it's incredibly noticeable.
-Very annoying to get stuck behind someone going up/down the stairs
-Stop the overlap between the phials and distillery at the alchemy bench 
-Why do people get so mad at whistling? Had a lot of folks ready to swing on me just for calling my horse

Shoutouts:
-Katherine. Good Lord. If you know you know. 
-Gamekeeper Vostatek
-Homie with the arrow in his head
-Devil's crew
-Capon
-Mutt and Pebbles

Possibly the Best RPG I’ve Ever Played – KCD2 is a Masterpiece in the Making

I didn’t expect Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 to grip me the way it has, but the more time I spend in its world, the more I realize just how deep and thoughtfully crafted this game really is. This isn't just another open world RPG with surface-level mechanics. KCD2 feels alive, layered, and incredibly immersive.

What really stands out is how every system in the game has weight and consequence. Combat isn’t button-mashing. it’s tense, methodical, and demands timing and skill. Dialogue options feel genuinely impactful. The way your choices ripple through the world and your relationships with NPCs is unlike anything I’ve seen in years.

It reminds me of Skyrim. Not in style, but in how it redefines what I expect from an RPG. Like Skyrim, KCD2 feels like a world I want to live in, not just play through. But where Skyrim leaned more toward fantasy and accessibility, KCD2 embraces realism and consequence. It's the kind of game where every skill learned, every decision made, and every encounter matters.

If you’re a fan of deep, immersive role-playing experiences that respect your time and intelligence, Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 might just be the best RPG you’ll play this decade. It certainly feels that way to me.

An excellent old school RPG, with solid mechanics and world exploring.

I never could get into the first KC:D game.  The combat was simply too frustrating to me, when even the initial tutorial proved difficult for me on my first play attempt.  Be reassured that this is NOT the case with KC:D2.  Early combat isn't as unforgiving, and you can quickly turn things around just by getting some armor.  For instance there is a side quest that involves having to fight through a pack of four or five wolves.  First time I tried with just some clothes on my back, I was getting two-shotted by them.  Put on a pair of metal gloves?  That made the fight totally trivial, as they kept trying to bite the very place that was very well protected.  So put on some armour, and combat becomes VERY manageable.

The writing and voice acting was in general excellent.  There are games where you have great voice acting from the main characters, and filler voices for NPCs.  That`s not the case in this game, each NPCs felt unique, and with its own character voice (but figuratively and literally).

The game offers a lot of side activities to do.  Personally, I made a lot of early money by spending hours at the Alchemy table.  The only drawback was having to wait 24 hours for merchants to get enough money to sell more of your inventory.  Overall, if you really want more money, there are various ways to get it.  The crafting mini-games are both very well done (blacksmithing and alchemy).  Having to actually follow a recipe to make potions was really engagning.

There's a LOT to explore in the world, lots of side quests to do as well.  Lot of fun Easter Eggs all over the place.  For instance I found a "vampire" corpse in a certain location.  You can also meet a very unique person if you wander on the road at night.  It all makes the world feel richer and more alive.

Overall, don`t base your evaluation of this game on its predecessor.  This one is better in every way, and should be evaluated on its own.  If you want to skip the first game (like I did), you can find a number of videos online that tell you the story of the first game so you are fully immersed into the storyline of this new game.

I'll almost certainly come back to this game even having finished it, once they launch the planned DLCs.  I'm not sure yet if I will start over again, or just continue from my last save.

One the best RPGs I've played in a while. Early on I killed a townsfolk outside of a tavern to regain my tin dice badge (dumb I know), left the spot for a couple weeks, and I thought I was alright. However, I was stopped by guards 2 in-game weeks later while fast travelling through the area. They tried to arrest me, my speech skills sucked at the time, so I ended up killing those guards too. Long story short, I learned early on that your actions had persistent consequences. This scales quite a bit as the game opens up, and that's one of my favorite mechanics in the entire game. The sword fights are brutal early on but with skill increases, better gear, etc you feel borderline invincible until an enemy jabs you in the one sweet spot your gear left vulnerable. Even then, by end game you have enough potions, perks, and strategies to mitigate anything in a fight. I'll end by saying that this is the first "long" RPG that I actually want to replay. It took me ~100 hours to complete my first play though and I left quite a few side quests untouched. I'm looking forward to playing again with the new hardcore mode.

Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 – A Medieval Masterpiece That Captivates the Soul

As an avid fan of immersive RPGs, Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 has been an absolute revelation. Warhorse Studios has not only refined the elements that made the original a cult classic but has elevated the experience to new heights, delivering a game that is both challenging and deeply rewarding.

A Living, Breathing World

The game's portrayal of 15th-century Bohemia is nothing short of breathtaking. From the bustling markets of Kuttenberg to the serene forests and imposing castles, every corner of the world feels meticulously crafted. The attention to detail is evident in the daily routines of NPCs, the dynamic weather systems, and the ever-changing landscapes that make exploration a joy.

Combat That Demands Skill and Precision

Combat in Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 is a true test of skill. The refined melee system requires precise timing, strategic thinking, and a deep understanding of each weapon's mechanics. Whether engaging in a one-on-one duel or fending off multiple adversaries, each encounter feels unique and consequential. The introduction of new weapons and enhanced AI ensures that no two battles are ever the same.

Deep Role-Playing Mechanics

The game's RPG systems are both intricate and rewarding. Skills improve through active use, encouraging players to engage with various gameplay elements to enhance their character’s abilities. The perk system offers further customization, allowing for different playstyles such as stealth, diplomacy, or brute force. This depth ensures that every decision feels impactful and personal.

Immersive Audio and Visuals

The visual fidelity of Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 is exceptional. The game's sharp 4K resolution, HDR support, and deep color output create a truly stunning medieval Bohemia. The lighting system and character animations add to the realism, making the world feel alive and reactive. Complementing the visuals is a masterfully composed soundtrack that enhances every moment, from the hustle of city streets to the tension of battle.

A Story That Resonates

The narrative continues the journey of Henry, the blacksmith's son, as he navigates a world filled with political intrigue, personal vendettas, and moral dilemmas. The story is rich, immersive, and deeply rewarding, with meaningful choices and natural dialogue that make every interaction feel significant.

Final Thoughts

Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 is a testament to the power of storytelling, attention to detail, and a commitment to delivering an authentic experience. It's a game that challenges you, immerses you, and leaves a lasting impression. For anyone who appreciates deep, narrative-driven RPGs, this is a journey you won't want to miss.
